title: US Initial Claims, Week Ending Jul 11
question: What will the U.S. Department of Labor report as the advance seasonally adjusted initial claims for unemployment insurance for the week ending July 11, 2026, first print?
resolutionSource: U.S. Department of Labor Employment and Training Administration Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims release
resolutionRule: Resolve to the advance first-print U.S. total seasonally adjusted initial claims figure, in thousands, for the week ending July 11, 2026, as published by the U.S. Department of Labor Employment and Training Administration in the Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims release dated July 16, 2026. Use the release's rounded thousand value; ignore later revisions and ALFRED/FRED vintage updates except as mirrors of the first official print.
drivers: Latest SA initial claims were 215 thousand, down 2 thousand from the revised prior week.
The 4-week average fell to 218.75 thousand, keeping the near-term level around the high 210s.
Seasonally adjusted continuing claims were up 8 thousand but broadly stable at 1814 thousand for the lagged week, not signaling a fresh layoff break.
July holiday-week adjustment can create noise, but the target is the SA advance print from the same DOL variant.

reasoning.text: Forecast for DOL SA Initial Claims, Week Ending July 11, 2026

Framing and exact resolver: the target is the U.S. Department of Labor Employment and Training Administration advance seasonally adjusted U.S. initial claims value, series code ICSA in the ledger, for week ending July 11, 2026, first print only. The DOL release dated July 16, 2026 is the resolver; FRED/ALFRED can mirror the vintage but is not the final authority.

reasoning.call: Opened the current DOL UI Weekly Claims PDF release at https://www.dol.gov/ui/data.pdf.
reasoning.result: The DOL release was embargoed until 8:30 A.M. Eastern on Thursday, July 9, 2026; for week ending July 4, 2026, advance SA initial claims were 215,000, down 2,000 from the prior week's revised 217,000.

reasoning.call: Read the national summary table in the same DOL release.
reasoning.result: The table reports Initial Claims (SA) of 215,000 for July 4, 217,000 for June 27, 216,000 for June 20, and 228,000 for the comparable prior-year week; the 4-week moving average was 218,750.

reasoning.call: Read the DOL continuing-claims and OUI data-page context.
reasoning.result: The DOL release reports seasonally adjusted insured unemployment of 1,814,000 for week ending June 27, up 8,000 from 1,806,000; the OUI weekly claims data page was updated July 9, 2026.

reasoning.text: Release-date check: the target week ending July 11, 2026 corresponds to the next weekly DOL UI Claims release dated Thursday, July 16, 2026 at 8:30 A.M. Eastern; the ledger may mirror that first print through ALFRED/FRED, but the official agency PDF is the resolver.

Variant check: every numeric anchor used here is the DOL seasonally adjusted U.S. initial claims variant from the weekly release, in thousands, matching the target unit and the ICSA-style target. NSA state totals such as 224,583 for July 4 are used only as qualitative context, not as target-history inputs.

Reference class and base rate: for the 2026 year-to-date SA initial-claims sequence through July 4, the level mostly sat in the 201-230 thousand range, with a recent 4-week average of 218.75 thousand. A persistence base rate around the latest 215 thousand is stronger than a trend-extrapolated jump because the latest four weekly changes were +5, -3, +1, and -2 thousand.

Prior/update/interval: persistence prior model on the DOL SA initial-claims level uses the January 3-July 4, 2026 historical sample of weekly changes: -6, +9, +1, +19, 0, -22, +3, +3, -1, -8, +6, -8, +15, -10, +7, -25, +9, +13, -2, +2, +13, +5, -3, -11, +1, -2 thousand. The average change is +0.3, so latest 215 + 0.3 gives 215.3; level/momentum adjustment is +0.5 for the still-low but slightly below-average latest print, one-off July-holiday noise adjustment is 0 after seasonal adjustment, and policy-mechanism adjustment is 0. Rounded point = 216. For interval sizing, sigma = 10.4 from those successive changes; 1.28*sigma = 13.3, rounded to a 14 thousand half-width, giving final implied bounds 216 - 14 = 202 and 216 + 14 = 230.

Counter-considerations: upside risk is a renewed education, transportation, or manufacturing layoff pulse like the prior large state moves, which would land above the interval if SA claims print above 230 thousand. Downside risk is another broad low-layoff week with holiday-seasonal factors absorbing NSA filings, which would land below the interval if the first print is under 202 thousand. Outside the interval would therefore require a weekly move larger than roughly the recent 80% one-week change range.

Review disposition: accepted the reviewer suggestions to clarify the July 16, 2026 DOL resolver versus ALFRED/FRED mirroring and to tighten the continuing-claims wording to up 8 thousand but broadly stable; no required fixes were identified.
